status: Individually reviewed candidate; public only after release verification
shape: A narrow, long-stiped mature study is distinct from broad X. polymorpha. The initial pair of symmetrical long pointed forks resembled regular antlers; one fork was removed, remaining fertile branches were shortened, thickened and made unequally nodulose, and abrupt shaft scaling was removed. A prepared section is explicitly separate from a white conidial appearance.
surface: Dark furrowed cortex and fine selected fertile papilla cues distinguish the mature exterior from pale cut tissue. The section-wall correction removes protruding black lump cues and later crescent occlusion. The complete authentic plate retains its different prepared and intact panels and original scale bars.
movement: Retained stationary mature stromata support an enlarged authored ascospore-drift overlay. White conidial coating, growth, germination and decomposition are not animated. This presentation does not merge a conidial stage with a mature sexual-form process.
residual: Branch junctions intersect rather than reproduce a measured continuous tissue union; the remaining fork is still regular. Basal hairs, exact nodules, conidiophores, perithecial walls and ascus microanatomy are incomplete. The prepared white core and ring walls are diagrammatic and unmeasured. Material response, hair density, natural stages, spore dimensions and flow are not calibrated. Close foci are partial anatomy views, and the edge-on front view occludes structures. This selected mature study is not a complete species-complex identification or life-cycle simulation.
assessment: Qualitative author assessment, not an accuracy score or independent scientific certification
